title: Services and Facades
readerIntent: Understand where reusable behavior and use-case coordination belong.
owner: Each capability owns its domain services; shared mechanics belong to Nodics service contracts
summary: Services perform reusable domain behavior; facades coordinate a use case across services; controllers remain transport adapters.

sections.heading: What is Services and Facades?
paragraphs: A service owns reusable business or technical behavior. A facade presents a stable capability boundary to controllers and other callers while hiding internal service composition and implementation changes.
Think of a customer-service counter backed by several specialist teams. Callers use one stable counter, while the internal assignment can evolve without changing every caller.

sections.heading: Business value
items: Keep one behavior reusable from APIs, jobs, events, workflows, imports, and assistants.
Override customer-specific behavior through later modules without copying callers.
Coordinate multi-service use cases without turning controllers into business owners.
Use one governed module-communication client with resilience and safe diagnostics.

sections.heading: Service responsibility
paragraphs: A service owns cohesive business or technical behavior. It receives normalized input and explicit context, enforces its invariants, uses owned models or provider-neutral capabilities, and returns normalized results.
Because transport details remain outside the service, the same behavior can be called by a controller, facade, workflow, scheduled job, event consumer, import process, or governed AI tool.

sections.heading: Facade responsibility
paragraphs: A facade coordinates one use case that requires several services or capability calls. It decides sequencing, aggregation, compensation, and the response-oriented result while each service retains its domain ownership.
A facade is not required for every route. Adding one that only renames a service call increases navigation and override complexity without adding responsibility.

sections.heading: Controller boundary
paragraphs: Controllers adapt HTTP or another transport: extract normalized input, delegate, and return the result for response handling. Authentication, tenant resolution, authorization, and request validation are coordinated by the request pipeline.
Business rules in controllers become inaccessible to jobs, imports, events, and other callers and therefore create duplicate behavior.

sections.heading: Example: publish approved content
paragraphs: A publishing facade can coordinate CMS content retrieval, workflow approval evidence, target publishing, cache invalidation, search updates, and audit. CMS, Workflow, Publishing, Cache, and Search services each retain their own contracts.

The facade must not write another module's collections directly or pretend several separate updates form one distributed transaction. It uses idempotency, compensation, and reconciliation where required.

sections.heading: Local and remote service calls
paragraphs: When the target module is active in the same process, the runtime may use local service resolution. When it is remote, the governed module transport resolves configured servers and calls the target API. The caller depends on the same capability result rather than provider or deployment details.
Human login tokens, internal service identities, and scheduled access remain separate trust paths.

sections.heading: Decision rule
items: Use a service for cohesive reusable behavior.
Use a facade when a use case coordinates several services or response concerns.
Keep domain ownership in the owning module even when a facade coordinates other modules.
Do not add a facade that only renames one service call.
Use pipelines or workflows when ordered processing or long-running manual and automatic actions exceed one synchronous use case.
Use a provider adapter when variation is external technology rather than business behavior.

sections.heading: Customization
paragraphs: A customer project first configures supported behavior. When the algorithm changes, a later module extends or overrides the smallest owning service or facade while preserving its public contract.
Two customer projects can customize independently. Neither edits reusable Nodics source or moves the rule into Axis.

sections.heading: Operational concerns
items: Bounded deadlines and cancellation propagation.
Retries only for safe reads or idempotent writes.
Circuit and pool behavior for remote dependencies.
Stable failures and safe causal context.
Metrics for latency, outcome, dependency, retry, and saturation.
Shutdown, in-flight work, and degraded dependency behavior.

sections.heading: Verification
items: Direct service contract and facade coordination tests.
API, job, event, workflow, import, and assistant integration.
Unauthorized and wrong-tenant behavior.
Timeout, retry, duplicate, partial failure, and compensation.
Default implementation and project override.
MonoServer and distributed topology regression.
